content_of_post_to_comment: Protip: the surname Rothschild, German for “red shield,” divides Roth-schild, not Roths-child. It’s also pronounced rote-shilt. (The h in roth is an archaic silent letter and wouldn’t be used in the modern German spelling rot.) Not that the kind of people who bring this surname up a lot care.
comment: A surname can become a kind of political Rorschach test: people hear what they already believe in it. The telling distinction is between being curious about a name's history and treating the name itself as evidence.
